file: papers/pdf/Merton and Barber - 2004 - The Qualities of Serendipity.pdf
about: This book chapter examines the linguistic qualities of the word 'serendipity': its oddity, whimsy, sound appeal and derived word forms. Along the way it notes how the word's meaning was defined and later broadened.

candidates.label: Happy accidental discovery
candidates.definition: Serendipity refers to making happy, unexpected discoveries by chance, that is, unplanned discovery that turns out favourably.
candidates.applies_when: An account describes coming upon something valuable or welcome that was not planned or sought, by chance.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The discovery was planned or deliberately searched for, or the chance event was not welcome or beneficial.

candidates.label: Serendipity as personal quality
candidates.definition: In Walpole's original sense, serendipity is a quality or gift that some people possess which enables them to make happy accidental discoveries, rather than the discovery itself.
candidates.applies_when: A person describes themselves or someone else as having a knack, gift or capacity for repeatedly stumbling on valuable things.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The account refers to a single fortunate event or found object rather than a person's enduring capacity; use the event/object type instead.

candidates.label: Serendipity as event or object
candidates.definition: Through use, the word came to cover the whole event of accidental discovery, and even the thing discovered, not only a quality of the discoverer.
candidates.applies_when: An account names a specific fortunate chance occurrence, or the thing found by chance, as 'a serendipity' or 'an instance of serendipity'.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The account attributes the discovery to a stable trait or knack of the person, which is the personal-quality sense.

candidates.label: Passive endowment vs active accomplishment
candidates.definition: The authors note an ambiguity in the actor's role in a happy accidental discovery. The discoverer can be seen as passively endowed with good fortune or as actively accomplishing the discovery.
candidates.applies_when: A narrator frames a chance discovery either as something that simply happened to them through luck, or as something they actively achieved, or wavers between the two.
